note: Known divergences that a check SEES, PRINTS, and does not fail on -- each one a decision somebody made on a date, with a date it stops being in force. Read by scripts/acknowledgements.py; see that module's docstring for the rule. The short version: the thing that expires is the ACCEPTANCE, never the finding. Before review_by the check is green and the item is counted in the summary line; after review_by the check is RED on 'this acceptance expired', which is a red a human can always close by deciding something. This file lives at the repo root and NOT under public/, because public/ is rsynced to production and this is CI metadata.
how_to_add_an_entry: Every field in scripts/acknowledgements.py REQUIRED_FIELDS is mandatory and non-blank, and `check` must appear in `checks` below -- the loader REFUSES the whole ledger otherwise, rather than skipping the entry, because a skipped entry reads to the next person as a real finding. Pick review_by per entry from when you actually expect to know more; do not give every entry the same date, or they all come due at once and the honest answer becomes a bulk re-accept, which is the same as having no clock.

policy.source: Chosen in PR ci/acknowledgement-clock (2026-08-09) as two working weeks -- long enough that the accepter sees EXPIRING SOON before the cliff and can act deliberately, short enough that the warning is not background noise. Not derived from measurement; revisit if warnings start being ignored.

checks.check-encoding-safety: scripts/check-encoding-safety.py -- the cp1252 preamble and encoding= sweep. Keys are repo-relative module paths, matching Finding.path.
checks.check-campaign-facts: scripts/check-campaign-facts.py -- the _facts_this_copy_must_not_break blocks in content/campaigns/. Keys are <campaign file>::<fact id> for entry-scoped findings, and <campaign file>::<finding name> for findings against the copy as a whole. NOTE: the `human` tier's review clock is NOT here -- it lives inline in the campaign file, next to the fact, because the person who acts on it reads that file and nothing else. This ledger holds only findings the check reports and somebody tolerates.

The claim understates rather than over-promises -- it sends someone away from a build that exists, which is a smaller harm than promising one that does not, but it is still wrong.
